decisions.title: Full spec, phased, approval gates between phases
Replace the tour page entirely at go-live; film player deleted
OpenAI TTS narration (ash) via existing pipeline; owner may record real VO later
All visitor-input features behind one shared moderation queue
Chicago Reporter CBL figures re-tiered reported; ids renamed to match verified values (155 renegotiated by Jul 1971, about 70 evicted, $14,000 average saved)
Whisper word-level cue alignment deferred to A4; sentence-proportional captions until then
A1 approved as-is; interaction grammar locked, A2 authorized
Self-review recommendations (immersive chrome, tighter cold-open crop, visible board labels) deferred to the A4 polish gate
Panel P1s fixed before the gate. explore-mode advisory wiring, ch1 chronology (two hundred years), ch2 pamphlet at the Haiti building (narration + voice card + Midway panel, TTS regenerated)

Panel P2s fixed at the gate. credit-line sanitizer, Shelley caption dated, cursor affordance + mode-card action cues, idle timer resets on wheel/scroll, countdown ring steps whole seconds under no-motion

Deferred to A3 and A4. off-screen countdown chip in HUD, ch5 era plate span, bombing docket row layout, dynamic-chunk loading blurbs, voices tray collect-verbs copy, audit extension to interactive aggregates, credits ingest sanitizing

Standing authorization to proceed autonomously through the phases with the quality system as the gate. Milestones self-approve when the verify suite, audits, and review panels are green (P1 and P2 findings always fixed first, P3 deferrals recorded). The owner ask is reserved for the C2 go-live swap that replaces the public film page.

A3 self-approved per standing authorization D-A2-04. 99 of 99 regression checks across 22 scenarios, all audits green, deferred P3 batch cleared. New finding carried to A4. the site navbar overlays the exhibit's top HUD strip at page top on desktop (merges with the immersive-chrome item).

Further citywide map cropping declined with rationale. The cold open's claim is citywide (find a neighborhood anywhere), so the frame must keep the whole city visible; the A2 tightening already made the Black Belt corridor legible, and the bombing map solves its own scale with a reprojection window.

A4 self-approved and phase A closed per D-A2-04. Full nine-lens panel ran on production; both P1s fixed (mobile HUD composed as one plated strip; universal redlining claims softened to the registry's corrected Black Belt scope with TTS regenerated) plus the full P2 batch (tour end plate, terminal final station, scoped explore playback, roving map tabindex, focus and announcement utility, HoldTheLine reword, credit formatter, figure recompression 6MB to 2MB, caption plating, dagger hit areas). Remaining P3s recorded. VO re-encode to 64 to 80 kbps folded into the phase B pipeline settings.

B1 self-approved per D-A2-04. Rigged Instrument system (four configs on documented instruments) and Machine Rooms M1 to M3 with the six-station floor plan, room overlay with hash deep links, doors in ch6, ch8, and ch9. 115 of 115 checks across 26 scenarios. Facts registered for the rooms, fair_housing_1968 and post_2008_return.

B2 self-approved per D-A2-04. Rooms for THE DEED and THE CODE, the counter-machine room with the Answer Key on registered facts, the gear train unlock, and machine cards. Strike the Clause ships as the static primary-text panel pending counsel review. Community build-back stories (Kimbark, Harper Court, the savings and loan) honestly plated as collection in progress pending sourced records. Galleries deferred to the sourcing effort.

C1 self-approved per D-A2-04. Visitor input pipeline live behind migration 008 (exhibit_submissions, RLS, 101-term screen, admin queue). The Answer Wall takes the honest migration-pending path until the owner applies supabase/migrations/008_exhibit.sql in the SQL editor, the same procedure as 006. Memorial and oral-history stations ship with the galleries; their API kinds are already supported.

Closing panel P1 and all eight P2s fixed before the swap ask. Answer Key contrast, bare room deep links, the wall's honest not-yet-collected stamp with focus management, the strike figure softened to about 500, the armor phrasing displayed as characterization pending its archival clipping, the room-close pause cue, the AA contrast token sweep, and the audio fleet re-encoded to 80 kbps mono (18.9MB to 9.8MB). P3s recorded for post-swap polish, including the HOLC map-year convention pass, room-content audit coverage, gear caption timing, spine tab stops, and the wall latency re-measure after migration 008.

GO-LIVE EXECUTED. The Ground Keeps Moving replaced the film page on chicago/hyde-park (owner chose the full swap). Film player deleted, media pruned to the poster, preview slug redirects with queries preserved, sitemap and indexing on, tag exhibit-live. Root-caused at the gate. the harness still pointed at the preview slug after a failed command chain, and the streamed redirect drops query strings, both fixed. Remaining owner action, apply migration 008 in the Supabase SQL editor to open the wall.

Owner verdict on v1, feels AI and gimmicky, like a kids game, confusing without context, remove the TTS voice, needs museum-grade education. Council diagnosis, the AI feeling is epistemological, simulations standing where real documents exist. Rebuild plan, one reader-paced experience (no audio, no modes, no auto-advance), delete the meta-game layer (medallion collectibles, machine board HUD, DECLINED tap game, press-and-hold, count-ups, gear train, answer key game, machine cards), rewrite all text as historian wall text per humanizer rules, keep only evidence-forward stations (real HOLC map with real surveyor sheets, bombing record, Two Buyers arithmetic, wealth gap scale, annotated real documents), add the Surveyor's Files reading room (576 real descriptions, permalinks), an opening context panel in plain words, and an About this exhibit authorship panel with the registry as bibliography. No visual-system redesign. Fact registry, HOLC data, and harness untouched as infrastructure.
